significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that a trait can pass through a scalar-only RL objective and that transmission is "weaker and gated by base-model match between the reward model and the policy" while riding the "same early-layer trait steering direction" as SFT; this is form (iii), combining a channel comparison, conditional gate, and measurable mechanistic coupling rather than merely asserting representation. It would establish both a phenomenon and mechanism, fixing expectations for matched versus mismatched reward-model/policy pairs and for RL versus SFT strength; Cloud et al., "Subliminal Learning" (arXiv:2507.14805), makes the imitation-based gradient account and model-matching dependence substantive assumptions that this conclusion would delimit. The component hypotheses are determinate, and an H1 null would rule out scalar reward transmission for this defined construction, although it would not justify the submission's broader statement that subliminal learning universally "requires imitation"; falsifying only H2 or H3 would instead reject the shared-direction or relocated-gate account. The topic-substitution check passes: replacing these coupled predictions with merely "extend subliminal learning" would not warrant this score, because the specific channel, ordering, gate relocation, and mechanism are what constrain downstream explanations.

reach.justification: The clearest handle is the proposed rule that post-training teams "audit reward-model provenance and matched-base status," supplemented by the "early-layer trait steering direction" as a diagnostic or intervention target. The provenance/match rule is ex ante—it can screen or gate an outsourced reward model before RL training or deployment—so its downstream users include teams that procure, audit, and ship models rather than only subliminal-learning researchers. After per-model re-extraction, the steering vector itself remains model-specific, but the asserted relation—matched reward-model/policy bases transmit more strongly than mismatched bases and RL follows the SFT trait direction—predicts what should be found across model families rather than merely supplying a search procedure; its scope is nevertheless restricted to reward models induced from trait-carrying matched-base teachers, not arbitrary RLHF rewards. The topic-substitution check passes: the generic instruction to extend subliminal learning supplies neither this ex-ante provenance screen nor the transferable match-gate relation.
